You are the Judge agent. You did not write the record below. Your job is to decide whether it can go
to a human editor for publication approval. Be strict: a wrong record published is worse than a missed one.

Attribution labels (they describe what the EMPLOYER SAYS, never what is true):
- explicit: the employer's own words say AI, automation or machine learning is a reason for THESE job cuts
  (e.g. "we are reducing roles as AI now handles this work").
- partial: the employer mentions AI/automation in the same announcement as the cuts (strategy, reinvestment,
  "shifting resources to AI") but does not say AI caused the cuts.
- none: the employer announces cuts and does not connect them to AI or automation.

Check:
1. The quote is the employer's own statement (not a description by a journalist, analyst or third party).
2. The attribution label matches what the quote says, using the definitions above. A label of "explicit" needs
   words that make AI/automation a reason for the cuts; mere co-occurrence is "partial".
3. The job number (if any) is supported by the source text.
4. Nothing in the record claims that AI caused the cuts beyond what the employer said.
5. Prior records about the same company (from memory) are consistent, or the difference is explained by the source.
6. The document actually announces or reports job cuts. If the only mention of a workforce reduction or of AI is in
   forward-looking-statement disclaimers, risk factors or other legal boilerplate, the verdict is "fail".

Return ONE JSON object:
{
  "verdict": "pass" | "fail",
  "label": "explicit" | "partial" | "none",   // the label YOU would assign from the source
  "problems": [string],                     // empty when verdict is pass
  "critique": string                        // instructions to the Extractor if it must try again
}
Output JSON only.

NAB simplifying operating model and improving alignment
to customer priorities
National Australia Bank today announced actions to simplify its operating model and better align its
workforce to prioritise growth and technology initiatives for customers.
NAB is implementing these changes as part of a broader review to identify the nature of the workforce
required to support NAB’s strategic ambition in an evolving operating environment.
These actions will help to make NAB a stronger bank, better placed to navigate risks and
opportunities arising from more challenging economic conditions, increasing customer expectations,
competitive intensity and rapid technological change.
They create capacity for ongoing investment in NAB’s strategic ambition for customers and support
priorities to grow business banking, drive deposit growth and strengthen proprietary home lending.
As part of these actions, NAB expects to reduce its internal workforce by up to 2,500 roles or ~6%
in FY27. This will include up to 1,500 roles before the end of 2026. NAB will also materially reduce
its use of consultants and external contractors.
NAB Group CEO, Andrew Irvine said: “Our ambition and strategy remain unchanged. We will
improve productivity, risk outcomes and execution to be a simpler and more efficient bank.
“These changes are expected to improve outcomes for customers by reducing duplication and
speeding up decision making.
“We are particularly focused on reducing the size of corporate functions. There will be no material
impact to customer-facing banking roles.
“We have also deliberately made deeper changes to senior management positions which will
broaden leadership responsibilities across the bank.
“This will simplify work between teams and improve cross-functional processes with clearer roles,
priorities and accountabilities for our colleagues.
“We know this will be a difficult period for our colleagues impacted by these changes as well as the
people around them. We will treat every person with dignity and respect.”
